disposition_reason: Two-page poster on a cocoa powder candidate reference material; concentrations appear only in a log-scale figure and the material is a reference material, not a market sample.

study.design: conference poster: multi-element characterisation of a cocoa powder candidate reference material
study.origin: imported cocoa powder (South Africa relies on West African and South American supply; origin of the candidate material not stated)
study.method: ICP-QqQ-MS after microwave digestion (9 mL HNO3, 1 mL H2O2, 0.5 mL HCl), external calibration with gravimetric internal standard
study.qa: wheat flour CRMs NIST SRM 1567b and NMISA CRM-0006; En-scores above 1 for Zn, Na, K, Ca (NIST) and Zn, Pb, Na (NMISA)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: International limits cited: Cd cocoa powder, Pb cocoa powder, Hg food

unresolved: All concentrations are shown only on a log-scale bar chart (Figure 2) with no printed values; nothing read off the figure.
The material is a candidate reference material, which the extraction rules exclude from findings in any case.
The poster states Cd is '200 times the EU limit' (which would be about 160 mg/kg), implausible for cocoa powder; no number printed.
Pb accuracy in the NMISA wheat flour CRM had an En-score of 3.78 (failed).
